rationale: C22 is a close drafting analogue: both are short executive orders whose sole operative function is to amend a specifically identified earlier directive at the paragraph level, using the formula that the provision “is hereby amended” and supplying replacement language introduced by “to read.” C21 and C19 also amend prior directives, but their amendment machinery appears within much larger, substantively unrelated instruments and is less similar to the child’s concise amendment form.

shared_material.child_excerpt: paragraph 1 of [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] of November 13, 1947 ... be, and it is hereby, amended to read as follows
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The penultimate paragraph of [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] of October 14, 1947 ... is hereby amended by changing the preceding quoted language to read
shared_material.explanation: Distinctively parallel operative formula identifying a provision of an earlier executive order and replacing its text.

shared_material.child_excerpt: 1. The Secretary of State ... and the Secretary of Labor are hereby designated to be members of the Board.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: changing the preceding quoted language to read “essential to (1) the supply and maintenance of the military or naval forces”
shared_material.explanation: Both orders immediately provide the new substantive wording that is to replace the identified earlier provision.
